23. Q: Why does the chapter emphasize that the reminder about death occurred on a normal night?
A: Show answer
The author points out that the Prophet ﷺ made the reminder during an ordinary night, not only during the last ten nights of Ramadan. This detail reinforces the idea that awareness of death and remembrance of Allah are not concerns reserved for special religious occasions. The chapter invites the reader to imagine hearing the address from home and to consider the emotional and spiritual effect it might have. The distinction also supports the earlier statement that meaningful conversations with the Companions occurred throughout the year. A normal night can therefore be a setting for serious reflection and instruction, even without the special context of the final nights of Ramadan.
Study instruction:
- Compare the ordinary-night reminder with the special Ramadan worship account and identify the lesson that applies throughout the year.

- The chapter’s nighttime teaching is not confined to Ramadan.

Q:** How does the reminder about death relate to the chapter’s broader message about the shortness of worldly life?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The author interprets the address as a reminder that earthly life is short and that people should not allow routine activities to obscure the reality of death and return to their Lord. By mentioning the trumpet blasts and repeating the statement about death, the Prophet’s ﷺ words direct attention beyond immediate concerns toward the Hereafter. 25. Q: What practical response does the chapter invite from someone who hears the Prophet’s ﷺ nighttime reminder?
A: Show answer
The chapter asks the reader to imagine being in Madinah and hearing the words from home, then consider whether the reminder would move them to pray and reflect on the final moments of life and the return to their Lord. This question turns the historical report into a personal exercise in self-examination. The point is not to claim that every listener would respond identically, but to examine whether awareness of death changes one’s priorities and conduct. A meaningful response would involve taking the reminder seriously, renewing remembrance, reviewing how time is used, and considering whether actions reflect the values one professes. The chapter frames this as spiritual reflection rather than a detailed prescribed routine.
Study instruction:
- Identify one practical change in remembrance, prayer, or use of time that follows logically from the reminder without claiming it is a new legal obligation.
Key point:
- The chapter turns the report into a personal invitation to reflect and respond.
- A reminder is most meaningful when it informs conduct and priorities.

Q:** What incident involving Usayd ibn Huḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr is narrated by Anas ibn Mālik?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>Anas ibn Mālik describes an incident in which Usayd ibn Huḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr sat with the Prophet ﷺ on a dark night. When they left him, two shining lights accompanied them and illuminated their path. When the two Companions separated to go to their respective homes, each had one light in front of him until he safely reached his destination. The chapter presents this as an extraordinary event connected with their time in the Prophet’s ﷺ company. It is distinct from the reports about night prayer and the verbal reminders. The account’s sequence matters: a shared gathering, two lights after departure, separation, and one light accompanying each person home.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Retell the incident in its correct order and identify the narrator, the two Companions, and what happened after they separated.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Anas reports two Companions being accompanied by lights after a nighttime gathering.<br>- Each received a light on the way home after they parted.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **27. Q:** Why does the chapter mention that the gathering with the Prophet ﷺ took place on a dark night?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The darkness provides the setting in which the two lights become especially noticeable and meaningful. The chapter says that the lights illuminated the Companions’ path after they left the gathering. Without the dark setting, the narrative contrast between the surrounding conditions and the shining lights would be less clear. The detail also explains why the lights were practically useful: they enabled the Companions to see their way as they travelled home. The passage does not provide an exact location, weather report, or technical explanation of the lights. It presents the darkness as part of the reported circumstances and invites the reader to recognize the extraordinary character of the event as described.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Identify which details establish the setting and which details describe the extraordinary event itself.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The dark night makes the illumination of the path central to the account.<br>- Do not invent physical or geographical details not supplied by the report.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **28. Q:** What happened to the two lights when Usayd ibn Huḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr separated?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>According to the chapter, the two lights initially accompanied the Companions after they left the Prophet ﷺ together. When they parted to reach their separate houses, each Companion had one light in front of him. The light continued to guide each person until he safely reached his destination. This detail gives the report a clear progression from one shared journey to two separate journeys, with illumination accompanying each individual. It also explains why the chapter does not simply say that a light appeared once and disappeared. The account describes assistance continuing after the Companions separated, while avoiding any further explanation of the lights’ physical nature beyond what is reported.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Draw a simple sequence of the shared departure, separation, and individual journeys, showing how the lights are described at each stage.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The two lights became one light for each Companion after they separated.<br>- The report says each light remained until its recipient reached home.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **29. Q:** What practical role did the lights play in the incident narrated by Anas?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter states that the lights illuminated the Companions’ path and remained before each of them until they safely reached their respective homes. Their practical role in the narrative is therefore guidance along a dark route. The author also interprets the event in a spiritual context and says it resembles how believers will be on the Day of Judgement. A careful answer should retain both aspects: the lights are described as illuminating the road in the immediate incident, and the author connects the event with a broader image of light associated with the Hereafter. The chapter does not give a scientific explanation or invite the reader to speculate about a mechanism for the lights.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Explain the immediate function of the lights and separately state the spiritual comparison made by the author.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The lights guided the Companions safely along their paths.<br>- The chapter also presents the event as resembling a future image of believers’ light.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **30. Q:** How does the chapter connect the lights accompanying the Companions with the Day of Judgement?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The author says that the incident strongly resembles how the believers will be on the Day of Judgement. This connection moves the reader from the immediate nighttime event to a broader spiritual image of guidance and light in the Hereafter. The chapter does not explain every detail of that future state or claim that the Companions’ experience was identical to it in every respect. It uses the incident as a resemblance that helps readers reflect on the spiritual significance of light and safe guidance. The distinction between the reported event and the author’s comparison should be preserved: the report describes what happened on the road, while the author draws a connection to the Hereafter.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Separate the narrative facts from the author’s interpretation and state precisely what is meant by the resemblance.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The author connects the nighttime lights with the image of believers on the Day of Judgement.<br>- A resemblance should not be expanded into an assertion of complete identity.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/al-qadr/1-5" target="_blank">Qur'an 97:1–5, Surah Al-Qadr</a></details> **31. Q:** What does the chapter mean by saying that companionship with the Prophet ﷺ could awaken the heart and soul?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The author describes the Prophet’s ﷺ heart as always awake and says that his beautiful state would enlighten and awaken the hearts and souls of those listening to him. This is devotional language about the effect of his presence, worship, and guidance. It suggests that the Companions’ gatherings were not merely social occasions; they could prompt remembrance, reflection, and renewed spiritual awareness. The chapter links this idea to the conversations and reminders described earlier. Readers should understand the statement as the author’s explanation of spiritual influence, not as a measurable physical process or a claim that every person experienced an identical reaction in every gathering.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Identify the chapter’s descriptions of spiritual influence and explain how they relate to the reported teachings and worship.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The author portrays the Prophet’s ﷺ example as spiritually awakening for those around him.<br>- The statement describes devotional influence rather than a measurable physical mechanism.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:554" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 554</a></details> **32. Q:** How does the chapter distinguish spiritual benefit from the extraordinary physical illumination described in the companions’ incident?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter first speaks of the spiritual benefit of sitting with the Prophet ﷺ: his worship and guidance could awaken the heart and soul. It then adds that, in some cases, a Companion might also be blessed with a shining light that illuminated the path. These are related but distinct ideas. Spiritual awakening refers to the effect of guidance and example on a person’s inner life, while the lights are part of a specific reported incident involving two Companions. The passage does not say that every gathering produced a visible light or that spiritual benefit always takes an extraordinary physical form. Keeping the distinction clear prevents a particular event from being turned into a universal expectation.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Compare the chapter’s language about an awakened heart with its concrete description of the two lights and explain why they should not be conflated.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Spiritual benefit and the reported visible lights are distinct aspects of the chapter.<br>- The extraordinary event is not presented as a routine result of every gathering.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **33. Q:** What does the chapter report about the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer on a night of Ramadan associated with Laylat al-Qadr?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter attributes to Ibn ʿAbbās an account of the Prophet ﷺ praying with the Companions on a night associated with Laylat al-Qadr, with mud, water, and tears described in the scene. The directly verifiable report that identifies the twenty-third night and traces of water and mud on the Prophet’s forehead and nose is Sahih Muslim 1168, narrated by ʿAbdullah ibn Unays. A related but distinct account in Sahih al-Bukhari 2016 is transmitted through Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. Neither of those two reports mentions tears in this incident. Unless a separate primary source for the Ibn ʿAbbās attribution and the tears is supplied, those details should be identified as the chapter’s secondary narrative rather than treated as established by Muslim 1168 or Bukhari 2016.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Summarize Ibn ʿAbbās’s account in order, including the setting, prostration, and signs observed after rising.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The account emphasizes humility, extended prostration, and tears during night prayer.<br>- The chapter identifies one reported occasion as the twenty-third night but widens the search to all ten final nights.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2016" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2016</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/al-qadr/1-5" target="_blank">Qur'an 97:1–5, Surah Al-Qadr</a></details> **34. Q:** What role does the cool and tranquil atmosphere play in the account of the Night of Power?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter describes the atmosphere as cool and tranquil and presents this as part of the remembered setting. That environmental detail is not stated in Sahih Muslim 1168, which reports the twenty-third-night rain and the traces of water and mud, nor is it a universal criterion established by the hadiths about Laylat al-Qadr. It should therefore be described as a detail in the chapter’s account, not as a test by which people can identify the Night of Power every year. The stronger, independently verifiable lesson is to seek Laylat al-Qadr across the last ten nights.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Distinguish a circumstance reported for one night from a general criterion that the chapter does not establish.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Coolness and tranquility are details of this particular account.<br>- The passage does not make them a universal identification rule for Laylat al-Qadr.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2020" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2020</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2021" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2021</a></details> **35. Q:** What does the account say about the Prophet’s ﷺ prostration on mud and water?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter reports that the Companions saw the Prophet’s ﷺ face directly prostrate on mud and water on the ground during the night prayer. The detail emphasizes the physical setting of the prayer and the humility expressed in prostration. It is not described as a staged demonstration or an attempt to avoid contact with the earth. The narrative draws attention to the reality of the ground beneath him and later notes that mud remained on his forehead and nose when he rose. The reader should retain these concrete details without inventing the composition of the ground, the amount of water, or other environmental facts that the passage does not provide.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Recall the physical details of the prostration and explain why the chapter includes them in the narrative.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The report specifically mentions mud and water on the ground.<br>- The detail reinforces the embodied humility of the act as described.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2016" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2016</a></details> **36. Q:** Why does the chapter emphasize that the Prophet ﷺ lengthened his sujūd during the night prayer?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter says that the Prophet ﷺ lengthened his prostration during the prayer. The primary reports most closely related to the mud-and-water incident, Sahih Muslim 1168 and Sahih al-Bukhari 2016, confirm prostration in water and mud and the traces left afterward, but they do not specify the duration of the prostration. The statement about lengthened sujūd should therefore be attributed to the chapter’s narrative unless a separate report is identified. Do not infer a precise duration or make it a universal measure for every person’s night prayer.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Connect the lengthened prostration to the other details in Ibn ʿAbbās’s account without inventing a precise duration.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Extended sujūd is a specific feature emphasized in the report.<br>- The chapter gives no numerical duration or universal timing rule.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2016" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2016</a></details> **37. Q:** What was visible on the Prophet’s ﷺ forehead and nose when he rose from prostration?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>According to the chapter’s account from Ibn ʿAbbās, mud was visible on the Prophet’s ﷺ forehead and nose when he rose from prostration. This observation follows the description of his face being placed directly on the mud and water on the ground. It confirms the physical setting of the prostration and gives the reader a concrete image of the scene. The detail should not be embellished with claims about injuries, discomfort, or the exact condition of the ground, because the chapter does not mention those matters. Its purpose is to preserve what the Companions observed and to reinforce the seriousness and humility of the worship described.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Recall the two locations where mud was observed and connect them to the earlier description of the ground.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Mud was seen on the forehead and nose after the Prophet ﷺ rose.<br>- The report does not describe injury or provide additional physical details.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2016" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2016</a></details> **38. Q:** What do the tears in Ibn ʿAbbās’s account add to the description of the Prophet’s ﷺ night prayer?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter says that tears were flowing from the Prophet’s ﷺ eyes in this account. However, Sahih Muslim 1168, the primary report that mentions the twenty-third night and mud on the forehead and nose, does not mention tears; Sahih al-Bukhari 2016 also describes mud and water without that detail. The tears may belong to another report or to the chapter’s secondary narration, but they should not be attributed to those two hadiths without separate evidence. A careful study answer preserves the chapter’s wording as the author’s account while clearly stating what the cited primary reports do and do not contain.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Explain how the tears complement the description of prostration while avoiding claims about unreported thoughts or causes.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Tears are an explicit detail in the account of the night prayer.<br>- The passage conveys devotion without specifying every inner experience.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2016" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2016</a></details> **39. Q:** Which night of Ramadan does the chapter associate with the particular incident narrated by Ibn ʿAbbās?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter associates its account with the twenty-third night of Ramadan. Sahih Muslim 1168 also describes rain on the twenty-third night and traces of water and mud after the prayer, but that report is narrated by ʿAbdullah ibn Unays, not Ibn ʿAbbās. The chapter’s attribution to Ibn ʿAbbās should not be merged with Muslim 1168. The safest presentation is to identify the chapter’s attribution as such and separately cite the independently verified Muslim report. The date of one reported incident does not establish that Laylat al-Qadr occurs on the twenty-third night every year.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- State the reported night and the author’s wider reminder in the same answer so that the specific event is not mistaken for an exclusive date.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The reported incident is associated with the twenty-third night in that year.<br>- The chapter says to seek Laylat al-Qadr throughout all ten final nights.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2020" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2020</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2021" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2021</a></details> **40. Q:** Why does the author caution readers not to restrict the search for Laylat al-Qadr to the twenty-third night?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The author explicitly says that the Night of Power should be sought on all the ten last nights of Ramadan and that a person should perform acts of worship throughout that timeframe. The specific incident narrated by Ibn ʿAbbās is associated with the twenty-third night in one year, but that report does not narrow the wider instruction. Confusing the date of one reported event with a rule for every year would overstate the evidence in the chapter. The author’s conclusion is practical: maintain worship across the final ten nights rather than relying on a single date. This preserves the distinction between a particular historical occasion and the broader guidance stated in the passage.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Explain the difference between the date attached to one report and the broader period the author says should be observed.<br>**Key point:**<br>- One reported occurrence on the twenty-third night does not narrow the search to that night alone.<br>- The chapter encourages worship throughout the final ten nights.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2020" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2020</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2021" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2021</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/al-qadr/1-5" target="_blank">Qur'an 97:1–5, Surah Al-Qadr</a></details> **41. Q:** How do the accounts of the last ten nights and the ordinary nighttime conversations complement one another?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The last-ten-nights account highlights intensified voluntary worship during a special period of Ramadan, while the other narratives show that nighttime teaching and reminders also occurred throughout the year. Together, they prevent an overly narrow reading of nighttime devotion. The Prophet’s ﷺ practice is presented as including sustained worship during the final ten nights and meaningful communication with the Companions on other nights. The reports about the full moon, remembrance of death, and the lights accompanying two Companions are examples of nighttime gatherings with different purposes and outcomes. The chapter therefore portrays night as a recurring setting for worship, guidance, reflection, and companionship, while retaining the special emphasis given to the last ten nights.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Create a comparison chart showing which incidents concern Ramadan worship and which are described as occurring on nights beyond that period.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The chapter combines a special Ramadan practice with year-round nighttime teaching.<br>- The reports should not all be assigned to the same night or occasion.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2024" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2024</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:554" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 554</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **42. Q:** What common themes connect the reports from ʿĀ’ishah, Jarīr, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Anas, and Ibn ʿAbbās?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>Each report highlights a different dimension of nighttime life in the Prophet’s ﷺ company. ʿĀ’ishah’s narration describes intensified worship and waking the family during the final ten nights. Jarīr’s account records a teaching about seeing Allah on the Day of Judgement, using the full moon as a comparison. Ubayy’s narration links qiyām with an urgent reminder to remember Allah and consider death. Anas reports the lights that accompanied Usayd ibn Huḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr after a nighttime gathering. Ibn ʿAbbās describes the Prophet’s ﷺ prostration, mud, and tears during a Ramadan night prayer. Together, the reports connect devotion, instruction, remembrance, companionship, and reflection on the Hereafter.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Match each narrator to the incident and identify the main theme contributed by that report.<br>**Key point:**<br>- The narrations provide different but complementary views of nighttime devotion and teaching.<br>- Accurate attribution helps prevent the incidents from being confused.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2024" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2024</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:554" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 554</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2457" target="_blank">Jami at-Tirmidhi 2457
- Sahih al-Bukhari 3805
- Sahih Muslim 1168
43. Q: Why is it important to keep the narrators and incidents distinct when studying this chapter?
A: Show answer
The chapter draws on several Companions, each associated with a different account. ʿĀ’ishah is cited for the practice during the last ten nights; Jarīr ibn ʿAbdullāh for the full-moon comparison; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb for waking after one-third of the night and addressing the people; Anas ibn Mālik for the lights accompanying two Companions; and Ibn ʿAbbās for the prayer on a night associated with Laylat al-Qadr. If these accounts are merged, readers may assign a statement to the wrong narrator or incorrectly assume that several events occurred on one occasion. Keeping the reports distinct supports accurate recall and responsible use of the chapter. It also helps the reader distinguish what is directly narrated from the author’s reflections connecting the incidents.
Study instruction:
- Make a narrator-event table and check that every quotation, action, and interpretation is assigned to the correct account.
Key point:
- Each Companion’s report contributes a distinct episode.
- Correct attribution is essential for accurate study and explanation.

- Sahih al-Bukhari 554
- Jami at-Tirmidhi 2457</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a></details> **44. Q:** How should readers distinguish a reported event from the author’s interpretation of its significance?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>A reported event is the narrative detail attributed to a Companion, such as the Prophet ﷺ waking his family, pointing to the full moon, addressing the people after qiyām, or being accompanied by Companions whose path was illuminated. The author’s interpretation explains why the event matters, such as reading “tighten his belt” as increased seriousness, connecting the lights with the Day of Judgement, or explaining the death reminder as a lesson about the brevity of life. Both are important, but they are not identical kinds of information. A careful student should identify the narrator’s report, then state the author’s explanation separately. This method prevents an explanatory comment from being misquoted as part of the original narration and makes the reasoning in the chapter easier to evaluate.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- For each major incident, write two short notes: what the narrator reports and what the author concludes from it.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Narrative evidence and explanatory interpretation should be kept distinct.<br>- Clear separation improves accuracy and prevents over-attribution.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:554" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 554</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a></details> **45. Q:** What is the most important overall lesson of Chapter 25, “Late Night Incidents With Him”?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The chapter presents nighttime as a period in which worship, remembrance, teaching, and reflection on the Hereafter come together. The Prophet ﷺ intensified his devotion during the last ten nights of Ramadan and woke his family. Other reports describe a full-moon teaching, a reminder about death, and light accompanying two Companions. The Ramadan mud report requires careful attribution: Sahih Muslim 1168 names ʿAbdullah ibn Unays for the twenty-third-night account, while Bukhari 2016 records a distinct report through Abu Saʿid al-Khudri; neither of those texts mentions tears. The Tirmidhi 2457 report also has a translation discrepancy about the time in the night and differing displayed grading notes. The lasting lesson is sincere devotion joined with accurate transmission and responsible study.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- Review the five narrations, explain their distinct lessons, and formulate a balanced summary that includes both the special last ten nights and year-round nighttime instruction.<br>**Key point:**<br>- Nighttime in the chapter is a setting for worship, guidance, remembrance, and reflection.<br>- The final ten nights deserve special attention, while the lessons extend beyond them.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2024" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2024</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1174" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1174</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:554" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 554</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a></details> **46. Q:** How do the mud-and-water reports in Sahih al-Bukhari 2016 and Sahih Muslim 1168 differ?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>Bukhari 2016 is transmitted through Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and describes the Prophet ﷺ telling those in i'tikaf to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten, followed by rain and prostration in mud and water. Muslim 1168 is narrated by ʿAbdullah ibn Unays and records rain on the twenty-third night, with traces of water and mud on the Prophet’s forehead and nose; the narrator says ʿAbdullah ibn Unays used to identify that night as the twenty-third. These reports are related in theme but are not the same chain or identical account. Their differences should be preserved rather than combined into one composite narration.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- "Make a comparison of the narrator, setting, timing, and physical details in the two hadiths."<br>**Key point:**<br>- Both reports connect night prayer with prostration in water and mud.<br>- The narrators and event details differ and should not be merged.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2016" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2016</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a></details> **47. Q:** What do Qur’an 17:79 and 32:16 add to the chapter’s accounts of night worship?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>Qur’an 17:79 refers to additional prayer during part of the night, while Qur’an 32:16 describes believers leaving their beds to call upon their Lord in fear and hope. Together, these verses provide a broader Qur’anic framework for the chapter’s hadith examples: night devotion is voluntary worship, supplication, and an expression of reliance on Allah. They do not specify that every believer must follow the Prophet’s exact Ramadan schedule or remain awake for a fixed number of hours. The verses should be read as guidance about the value and spirit of night devotion, alongside the specific Prophetic reports.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- "Read both verses in context and identify the actions and spiritual attitudes each passage emphasizes."<br>**Key point:**<br>- The Qur’an connects night devotion with additional prayer and supplication.<br>- Fear, hope, and reliance are part of the devotional attitude described.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://quran.com/al-isra/79" target="_blank">Qur'an 17:79, Al-Isra</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/as-sajdah/16" target="_blank">Qur'an 32:16, As-Sajdah</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/en/al-muzzammil" target="_blank">Qur'an 73, Surah Al-Muzzammil</a></details> **48. Q:** How should Muslims seek Laylat al-Qadr without relying on weather or other unverified signs?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The sound approach is to follow the Prophetic instruction to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights, with particular attention to the odd nights, rather than using a single weather pattern as a universal test. Muslim 1168 records rain during one report associated with the twenty-third night, but that circumstance describes the particular incident. Bukhari 2020 directs people to seek the Night of Qadr in the last ten nights, and Bukhari 2021 mentions odd nights. A person should therefore maintain worship throughout the period and avoid turning one report’s conditions into a checklist that claims certainty about the night every year.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- "Plan worship across the last ten nights and identify which details are general instructions and which belong to one historical incident."<br>**Key point:**<br>- The general instruction is to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights.<br>- Weather in one report is not a universal identification test.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2020" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2020</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2021" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2021</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/muslim:1168" target="_blank">Sahih Muslim 1168</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/al-qadr/1-5" target="_blank">Qur'an 97:1–5, Surah Al-Qadr</a></details> **49. Q:** What is the difference between an extraordinary sign and a normative act of worship in the chapter?<br><details><summary><strong>A:</strong> Show answer</summary><br>The lights accompanying the two Companions are reported as an extraordinary event, whereas night prayer, remembrance, and seeking Laylat al-Qadr are practices supported by broader Qur’anic and Prophetic guidance. An exceptional sign can illustrate the merit of particular people or a moment of divine assistance, but it does not create a routine that every worshipper should expect or attempt to reproduce. Normative worship is established through general instructions and recurring Prophetic practice. Keeping the categories separate prevents readers from treating a miracle as a required spiritual outcome or from measuring their devotion by whether an extraordinary event occurs.<br>**Study instruction:**<br>- "Classify each chapter incident as a general devotional practice, a specific teaching, or an extraordinary reported event."<br>**Key point:**<br>- The light incident is an exceptional report, not a routine worship requirement.<br>- General devotional practices require their own evidence and should not be inferred from miracles.<br>**Source links:**<br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3805" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 3805</a><br>- <a href="https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2024" target="_blank">Sahih al-Bukhari 2024</a><br>- <a href="https://quran.com/en/al-muzzammil" target="_blank">Qur'an 73, Surah Al-Muzzammil</a></details> **50. Q:** How should a student verify the wording, timing, and grading of the Ubayy ibn Kaʿb report in Jami at-Tirmidhi 2457?
A: Show answer
A careful student should read the Arabic text, compare the published translation, and record the grading statements separately. The Arabic wording on the cited page says that two-thirds of the night had passed, while the English rendering says one-third had passed. The same page reproduces Imam al-Tirmidhi’s statement that the report is hasan and also displays a later Darussalam grade of da'if. These are distinct editorial or scholarly evaluations and should not be collapsed into a single claim of unanimous grading. The report should be cited with its collection and number, and any discussion of its precise timing or authenticity should acknowledge these differences.
Study instruction:
- "Record the Arabic phrase, the English translation, the compiler’s note, and the displayed later grade in separate fields."
Key point:
- The Arabic and English timing on the page differ.
- Tirmidhi’s own grading note and the later displayed grade should be reported separately.

- Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2457
- Qur'an 79, Surah An-Nazi'at
